# 1.3 Normed Spaces

**Fig. 1.11** Cone generated by a set $S$ (see [72, Fig. 4.3])

![](bbox=[0.485, 0.093, 0.875, 0.273])

**Definition 1.11** Let $S$ be a nonempty subset of a real linear space. The set

$conc(S) :={\lambda s \mid \lambda \geq 0 \text{ and } s \in S\}$

is called the cone *generated by S* (Compare. Fig. 1.11).

If a real linear space is preordered, then a preorder can also be introduced on its dual space.

**Definition 1.12** Let $Y$ be a real linear space with a preorder cone $C$. The cone

$C' :={\ell \in Y' \mid \ell(y) \geq 0 \text{ for all } y \in C\}$

is called the dual cone for $C$ (here $Y'$ denotes the algebraic dual space of $Y$).

# 1.3 Normed Spaces

Although normed spaces are the most important space structure in the second part of this book, we first start with topological spaces in general.

**Definition 1.13** Let $Y$ be a nonempty set.

+   (a) A topology $\mathcal{T}$ on $Y$ is defined to be a set of subsets of $Y$ that satisfy the following axioms:

+   (i) Union of sets of $\mathcal{T}$ belongs to $\mathcal{T}$.

+   (ii) Finite intersection of sets of $\mathcal{T}$ belongs to $\mathcal{T}$.

+   (iii) $\varnothing \in \mathcal{T}$ and $Y \in \mathcal{T}$.

In this case, $(Y, \mathcal{T})$ is called a topological space and the elements of $\mathcal{T}$ are called open sets.

+   (b) Let $\mathcal{S}$ and $\mathcal{T}$ be two topologies on $Y$. $S$ is called *finer than* $\mathcal{T}$ (or $\mathcal{T}$ is called *coarser than* $S$) iff every open-set is $\mathcal{S}$-open.
